title: HeatGuard Agent — Visual World Direction
question: The roll assigned Mission Control Console. Keep it, take the Surveyor's Total Station (Impeccable's Pick), take a challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: Mission Control Console
options.lineage: NASA MCC, SpaceX Hawthorne, ESA ESOC — where 'Go for launch' is a recorded, defensible decision by named officers
options.thesis: The dashboard is a flight director's console: event timeline, telemetry strips, anomaly flags — the PROCEED/MODIFY/RESCHEDULE call is a GO/NO-GO poll with authority.
materials: green GO / red NO-GO / amber HOLD
options.type: JetBrains Mono for all telemetry, IBM Plex Sans for officer labels, Space Grotesk for headers
options.viewport: Landscape console. Top 20%: event timeline (horizontal, newest right). Middle 60%: three vertical strips — LEFT: map with AOI, CENTER: temperature trend sparkline with threshold bands, RIGHT: climate zone + thresholds. Bottom 20%: DECISION POLL — large GO/HOLD/NO-GO buttons, officer ID (supervisor name), timestamp, voice loop indicator (Slack). Recommendation/reason in CAPCOM strip.
options.risk: The console density can overwhelm. The decision poll must be the visual climax — everything else supports it. Mobile requires collapsing to single-strip scroll.

raised.raise: Hazard-stripe threshold bands on the temperature sparkline — the isotherm diagonal crosses the trend when risk breaches MEDIUM/HIGH
Split-flap animation on the decision poll — GO/HOLD/NO-GO cascades character-by-character like a concourse board, making the call unmissable
Variable-font weight axis on the decision badge — the word PROCEED/MODIFY/RESCHEDULE thickens from Regular to Black as confidence rises
Carbon-copy memo styling for recommendation/reason — the CAPCOM strip reads like a filled flight coupon, authoritative and archival
Particle-mote ambient background in the console void — subtle depth cue that the timeline strips float in, reinforcing the 'room' metaphor

options.label: Surveyor's Total Station
options.lineage: Leica, Trimble, Topcon total stations — the instrument supervisors respect for 'this is where the line goes'
options.thesis: The dashboard is a precision surveying instrument: clean grid, monospace angular readouts, hierarchical data density — every pixel serves the measurement.
options.type: Monospace for all measurements (JetBrains Mono), UI labels in Space Grotesk at 11px
options.viewport: Center: map with crosshair and bearing rings. Right: stacked readout panels — Site ID, Climate Zone, Peak/Avg Temp, Decision (large), Recommendation. Bottom: status bar with satellite count, battery, time.
options.risk: Can feel too sparse for a dashboard that needs to show reasoning text. The recommendation/reason fields need breathing room without breaking the instrument density.

options.label: Industrial Streetwear Grammar
options.thesis: Ordinary words set in straight quotation marks, zip-tie tags left on, diagonal hazard stripes crossing white cotton and black nylon.
options.type: Bold industrial caps inside straight quotation marks, label plates set square on the grid like stenciled crates
options.viewport: Hazard-stripe diagonals (45deg) as section dividers. Every label wrapped in straight quotes via ::before/::after. Active zone keeps orange zip-tie tag. Decision badge = large quoted word with hazard stripe behind it.
options.case: Fuses well: hazard stripes become threshold bands on the temperature sparkline; quoted labels map to climate zone badges. Loses on authority — reads as style over instrument.
options.kept: Hazard-stripe threshold bands on the temperature sparkline — the isotherm diagonal crosses the trend when risk breaches MEDIUM/HIGH

options.label: Mesophotic Deep Dive
options.thesis: A technical deep dive down a volcanic island wall — one small diver crosses a thermocline into a mesophotic garden of black coral and marine snow.
options.type: Monospaced dive-computer digits for depth/gas beside quiet grotesk notes, one vertical depth axis ruling every line
options.viewport: Vertical depth profile as primary navigation. Surface → thermocline → reef ledge → mesophotic wall → turnaround → ascent. Temperature trend = depth profile. Decision = turnaround depth marker.
options.case: Fuses poorly: construction supervisors don't identify with dive profiles. The vertical metaphor fights the map's horizontal nature.
options.kept: Single thermocline cyan band as the active threshold marker — a clear line between 'above' and 'below' safe limits

options.label: Rail Concourse Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Cascading letter flaps, platform columns, and departure rhythm hold a thousand travelers in one gaze.
options.type: One condensed white sans on every flap, characters in fixed cells, destinations in caps
options.viewport: Split-flap board as the decision display. Rows = evaluations ranked by time. Columns = Site, Zone, Peak, Avg, Decision. The decision column flaps PROCEED → MODIFY → RESCHEDULE.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: evaluations map to rows; decision column is the departure status. Holds clarity. Loses on spatial mapping — the map and board live in different visual languages.
options.kept: Split-flap animation on the decision poll — GO/HOLD/NO-GO cascades character-by-character like a concourse board, making the call unmissable

options.label: Variable Font Specimen
options.thesis: A single giant letter fills the screen. Drag the weight slider and it thickens from hairline to black under your finger.
options.type: The specimen face at enormous display size against tiny monospace UI labels; strict measure and baseline grid; hierarchy by scale contrast alone
options.viewport: Decision word (PROCEED/MODIFY/RESCHEDULE) at hero scale, driven by font-variation-settings. Slider = confidence axis. Grid of all glyphs breathes in step below.
options.case: Fuses beautifully on the decision badge: variable weight = decision confidence. Loses on information density — a specimen shows one thing, a dashboard shows many.
options.kept: Variable-font weight axis on the decision badge — the word PROCEED/MODIFY/RESCHEDULE thickens from Regular to Black as confidence rises

options.label: Jet-Age Airline Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Red carbon numerals, a fold-out route arc, a stapled baggage stub — the whole Atlantic crossing fits in a paper wallet.
materials: red over crisp white coupon stock
options.type: Airline grotesk caps on tabbed coupon heads, fare boxes ruled in hairlines, carbon numerals striking fixed fields
options.viewport: Coupon book flow. Each evaluation = one coupon leg. Site/Zone/Temp/Decision = fixed fields on the coupon. RESCHEDULE = red VOID stamp. History = torn coupons in wallet.
options.case: Fuses on authority: filled coupons are archival records. The carbon-copy memo for recommendation/reason transfers perfectly. Loses on live feel — coupons are static, our data is live.
options.kept: Carbon-copy memo styling for recommendation/reason — the CAPCOM strip reads like a filled flight coupon, authoritative and archival

options.label: Sixth-Gen System Menu
options.thesis: Memory towers drifting like monoliths in fog, cubic rooms of ambient particle light standing in for chrome.
options.type: Sparse thin sans labels floating beside objects, no panels or rules, composition is objects arranged in depth
options.viewport: 3D console void. Three floating panels (map, telemetry, decision) drift in fog. Selection swells panel forward. Particle motes indicate depth.
options.case: Same catalog ID as assigned direction — this IS the assigned world's source. The assignment fused it with Mission Control grammar.
options.kept: Particle-mote ambient background in the console void — subtle depth cue that the timeline strips float in, reinforcing the 'room' metaphor

canonCard.label: Standard Dashboard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships — clean cards, data tables, status badges — executed at impeccable craft.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects: header, search, map left, decision card right, history below. At full fidelity: precise spacing, perfect contrast, smooth motion.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design. No mechanism demonstration.
